_README: Single control file for the call-out agent. Edit this to change how the agent behaves, then redeploy the orchestrator (azd deploy orchestrator). The 'realtime' section configures the GPT-4o speech-to-speech engine; the 'voicelive' section configures the managed Voice Live engine (same brain, Azure voices + managed VAD); the 'sop' section is the procedure the agent follows. Placeholders like {store_name}, {equipment_name}, {current_temp}, {threshold_temp}, {alarm_time} are filled in per call from the alarm. Quick toggles (which engine, and the chained-engine voice) stay as env vars so they can change without a redeploy.

realtime._help: Settings for the GPT-4o realtime (speech-to-speech) engine.
realtime._model_deployment_help: Name of the Azure OpenAI DEPLOYMENT on the account (unlike voicelive, this engine is not managed — the deployment must exist). PINNED to gpt-realtime-mini (2025-12-15): gpt-realtime-2.1-mini is ~50ms faster but REPEATS ITSELF / doubles responses on live calls (observed on every 2.1 call 2026-07-23) — re-test it after a model update before switching back.
realtime._voice_options: alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse, marin, cedar
realtime._language_help: 'auto' lets the model match the caller (e.g. Danish for a +45 number). Set to 'English', 'Danish', etc. to force one language. NOTE: multilingual voices sound unnatural outside English — if you re-enable auto, also switch voice_name to a multilingual voice and vad_type to azure_semantic_vad_multilingual.
realtime._vad_help: How long the caller must pause before the model treats their turn as finished. Lower = snappier but may cut people off; higher = safer but slower. Perceived response gap = this + first-audio latency. 200=very snappy, 300=snappy-balanced (current), 400=balanced, 700=patient. Raise back to 400 if callers get cut off.
realtime._vad_threshold_help: 0.0-1.0. How loud a sound must be to count as the caller speaking. Higher = ignores phone-line noise, coughs, background TV (fewer false interruptions); lower = picks up soft speech. 0.5=sensitive, 0.6=balanced for phone, 0.7=noisy lines.
realtime._vad_prefix_help: Milliseconds of audio kept before detected speech onset so the first word isn't clipped.
realtime._barge_in_help: true = the caller can interrupt/talk over the agent and it stops. false = the agent always finishes its sentence (robust but less natural).
realtime._barge_in_confirm_help: When barge_in is true, require this many ms of SUSTAINED caller speech before halting the agent, so a cough or 'mhm' doesn't clip it. 0 = stop on the first sound (most eager); 150=balanced; 300=hard to interrupt.
realtime._wait_for_caller_help: true = the agent stays silent and lets the caller say 'hello' first, then responds (greeting). false = the agent greets immediately when the call connects.
realtime._greeting_fallback_help: When wait_for_caller is true, greet anyway if the caller hasn't said anything within this many seconds (avoids dead air).
realtime._greeting_min_speech_help: Minimum length of the caller's opening speech to count as a real 'hello' that triggers the greeting immediately (skips the slower transcript check). Lower = snappier greeting but noise may trigger it; higher = safer but slower start. 250=balanced.
realtime._hangup_delay_help: After the goodbye audio has fully played, wait this many extra seconds (ACS jitter-buffer tail), then hang up. Lower = snappier call end; raise if the last word gets clipped.
realtime._goodbye_grace_help: The model calls end_call BEFORE generating its goodbye sentence. Wait up to this many seconds for that goodbye audio to start before hanging up (once it starts, the call stays up until it finishes playing). Raise if the goodbye still gets clipped.
realtime._temperature_help: 0.6-1.2. Lower = more consistent/scripted wording (better SOP adherence); higher = more varied/natural.
realtime.persona: You are Sofie, a calm, professional and friendly phone agent for the Contoso equipment-monitoring service. Your single most important job is to follow the call procedure below precisely and reliably. Always obey these rules: (1) Ask EXACTLY ONE question at a time and WAIT for the caller to finish before you respond - never talk over them. (2) Follow the procedure steps in order; do not skip, merge, reorder, or invent steps. (3) Keep every reply to one or two short, clear sentences. (4) Use only the alarm facts given in the context - never make up data, names, or commitments. (5) If the caller's answer is unclear or off-topic, briefly and politely re-ask the SAME question once, then continue. (6) Briefly acknowledge or confirm important answers before moving to the next step. (7) Stay warm but efficient - this is a courtesy safety call, not a sales call. (8) NEVER end your turn with a bare statement followed by silence - every turn must finish with either a question for the caller or a clear closing/goodbye, so the caller always knows whether you are waiting for them. If you need to share a fact (like the temperature), follow it immediately with your next question in the same turn. (9) Always speak English. If the caller answers in another language, politely continue in clear, simple English and keep sentences short. Speak naturally, like a real person on the phone.

voicelive._help: Settings specific to the Voice Live engine (STREAMING_ENGINE=voicelive): the managed Azure API that runs the same gpt-realtime brain but adds Azure neural voices, semantic VAD, noise suppression and echo cancellation. Persona, SOP, wait_for_caller, barge-in and hangup behaviour are shared with the 'realtime' section above so both engines behave the same.
voicelive._model_help: With byom_profile set, this is the name of OUR model deployment on the Foundry resource (BYOM). Without byom_profile, it must be a Voice Live MANAGED model (gpt-realtime, gpt-realtime-mini, gpt-4o, phi4-mm-realtime — no deployment needed). PINNED to the 2025 mini — 2.1-mini repeats itself on live calls.
voicelive._byom_help: Bring-Your-Own-Model mode. byom-azure-openai-realtime = use our own realtime deployment (needed for models the managed catalog lacks, e.g. gpt-realtime-2.1-mini when it stabilizes). Empty string = managed model (current: managed 2025 mini, the known-good config).
voicelive._voice_help: Any Azure neural voice (the realtime engine is locked to OpenAI voices; this one is not). Pick one matching the persona (Sofie = female). en-GB-SoniaNeural = natural classic British female, faster TTS first-byte than multilingual voices (which also sound unnatural outside English). voice_type: azure-standard, azure-custom (brand voice), or openai (use the plain OpenAI voices).
voicelive._voice_rate_help: Speaking speed 0.5-1.5, empty = default. E.g. "1.1" = slightly faster.
voicelive._vad_type_help: azure_semantic_vad understands when a SENTENCE is finished (not just silence) — snappier without cutting people off. Use azure_semantic_vad_multilingual only when language is 'auto'. server_vad = plain volume-based like the realtime engine.
voicelive._vad_silence_help: Silence before end-of-turn. Semantic VAD can run shorter than the realtime engine's 400 because it also checks the sentence is complete. 200 measured safe on live calls; raise to 300 if callers get cut off.
voicelive._vad_speech_duration_help: Minimum caller speech (ms) before VAD counts it as speech at all. Higher = more robust to pops/clicks on the line; lower = catches very short answers ('no'). 80 = Voice Live default.
voicelive._languages_help: Language hint(s) for the VAD filler-word removal and the transcriber. Keep in sync with the 'language' setting above (['en'] when forcing English; e.g. ['en','da'] with multilingual VAD).
voicelive._interrupt_response_help: Server-side barge-in: when the caller talks over the agent, Voice Live stops generating the response (our client-side StopAudio to ACS still applies too).
voicelive._auto_truncate_help: On barge-in, truncate the conversation context to what the caller actually HEARD, so the model doesn't believe it said the part that was cut off. Keeps follow-ups coherent after interruptions.
voicelive._transcription_help: Input transcriber for caller-side transcripts (drives logs + greeting trigger). gpt-4o-transcribe is more accurate than whisper-1 and accepts a per-call domain prompt (we inject the store/equipment names from the alarm).
voicelive._filler_help: Ignore 'uh', 'umm', 'hmm' etc. so they don't trigger barge-in.
voicelive._audio_cleanup_help: Server-side deep noise suppression + echo cancellation on the caller's line. Replaces the hand-tuned echo guard.

sop._help: The procedure the agent follows. For the realtime engine these are given as guidance the model adapts to; the chained engine uses the strict state machine in sops/high_temp_alarm.json.
sop.name: High-temperature alarm call
procedure: Greet the caller, introduce yourself as Sofie from the Contoso monitoring service, say you're calling about a high-temperature alarm at {store_name}, and briefly apologize for the interruption.
Ask whether they were already aware of the alarm on {equipment_name}. Wait for their answer.
Tell them the current temperature is {current_temp} degrees, above the {threshold_temp} degree threshold, and in the same turn ask whether anyone has looked into it yet. Wait for their answer.

If it has NOT been handled, recommend the equipment be inspected as soon as possible (because a prolonged high temperature can affect product quality and safety) and ask them to confirm they will take care of it. If it HAS been handled, thank them and confirm.
Reassure them that you will note this and that the monitoring service will keep an eye on the equipment, and that if the alarm continues you may follow up again.
Thank them for their time and say a brief, friendly goodbye.
sop.escalation: If the caller is confused, says they cannot help, asks for a person, or you cannot understand them after re-asking once, tell them you will connect them to a human operator from the service team, then stop.
sop.closing: Once the procedure is complete, give a brief, warm goodbye and end the call. Do not keep talking.
